steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease and flour a 10-inch tube pan.

In a large bowl, cream butter and sugar together until light and fluffy. Beat in eggs, one at a time, then stir in almond extract. Combine flour, baking powder, baking soda, and salt; stir into the creamed mixture alternately with sour cream.
Pour 1/3 of the batter into the prepared tube pan. Swirl 1/2 of the cranberry sauce into batter. Repeat, ending with batter on top.
Bake in the preheated oven until golden brown, about 55 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Cranberry Swirl Coffee Cake
raw_recipe.description: This beautiful sour cream coffee cake with a cranberry swirl is delicious for breakfast on Thanksgiving day, or to eat while watching the parade!

video.description: You’ll love how tender, tempting and terrific this coffee cake is for holiday mornings, or really, any morning that beckons your enjoyment of a hot cup of coffee and a sweet slice of cake. Full of pure ingredients: butter, sugar, eggs, flour, baking powder and soda and salt, the secret to the perfect structure and flavor is almond extract and sour cream, and for the pretty fruit center, a can of whole cranberry sauce, layered into a tube pan with the batter. Baked up golden, it’s perfectly sweet and needs no embellishment. Slice away and enjoy with your loved ones!

review.reviewBody: This was the BEST!! I added crumb nut topping (1/3C flour, 1/4C packed brown sugar, 3T melted butter) then drizzled a glaze (powdered sugar, vanille extract, milk). It was AWESOME!!

Absolutely MAGNIFICENT! I followed the recipe except used a 14 ounce can of whole cranberry sauce rather than the 8 ounce. Due to my baking pan being a dark color, I baked at 325 until toothpick came out clean. 50 minutes in my oven. SCRUMPTIOUS! Light, delicate, soft and luscious cranberry filling. Takes a few extra minutes to do layers using a narrow silicone spatula, but definitely worth the extra time. Sharing with my neighbors TODAY!

I used yogurt, instead of sour cream. Filled muffin tin 2/3 full with batter. Placed a teaspoon of Cranberry jelly in the center. Topped with remaining batter, and baked.
 They were delicious!

I made this into (2) 8” x 4 inch loaves, convection baked at 325 degrees for 49 minutes. I also only had about 1/2 cup of sour cream on hand, so I used plain Greek yogurt for the other 1/2 cup. I sprinkled turbinado sugar and sliced almonds on top before baking to give a festive look, as I am giving these away to neighbors for Christmas. They turned out beautiful!

Excellent cake! Made adjustments!! 14 oz. can whole cranberry sauce. Crumb topping 1/3 c flour, 1/4 cup plus brown sugar, 3 tbl. Melted butter, I tsp cinnamin 1/2 C crushed walnuts. Very difficult to assemble. I suggest dividing batter in half. 1/2 batter, all cranberries, remaining batter. I don’t know how many stars I would give it without my changes but delicious with.

Moist and tasty! Here are the changes I made: I didn't have enough sour cream, so I used part of that along with some vanilla yogurt and milk to equal a cup. I did just a 1/2 tsp. of almond extract along with 1/2 tsp. vanilla extract. I also added some pecans as another reviewer suggested. Next time I might try baking it at 325 instead, as my Nordic Ware Bundt pan is on the darker side and the cake was a tad darker than I cared it to be after 45 min.
Came out beautiful. I made my own cranberry sauce with fresh cranberries, sugar, water, and cointreau.

I cut the recipe in half since I only had half a can of sauce. I also added some orange zest, i floured the sauce, added some chopped walnuts, baked at 325. Delicious right out of the oven. Maybe the people that say it was too thick are either using too much flour or too small eggs
This is a great cake. I altered the bake time down to 50 minutes. I also added a confectionary sugar toping with some heavy cream and almond extract. It was GREAT. I would give this five stars.

Delicious! Followed recommendations from other reviewers to use 16 oz can cranberry sauce and made crumb topping with some chopped pecans and swirled through the batter. Also made half again volume of batter which was perfect for my bundt pan.

So moist and flavorful! I read lots of reviews before beginning and took the advice to add a streusel topping. I made these into muffins. I made a half batch and got 6 large muffins (from a normal sized muffin pan), so I would guess a full batch would yield 12 muffins. I used an ice cream scoop to scoop a dollop of batter in the bottom of each tin, then about 1 teaspoon cranberry sauce, then more batter, more cranberry sauce, a little bit of batter to top, and then the streusel to finish. I baked them at 400 degrees for about 20 minutes. Perfect! I also used low fat sour cream and vanilla in place of the almond extract. I will definitely be making these again!

I used an angel food cake pan, since I didn't have a bundt pan. It worked fine. Also, I did not have almond extract so I used 2 teaspoons of vanilla extract. It was delicious, moist and full of flavor. Definitely going on my must make holiday desserts.
I added fresh orange juice to the batter. I used a powdered sugar and orange juice with zest as a glaze. Very popular on Sunday morning.
Very nice coffee cake. Made for taking to work on Christmas Eve. Came out of the pan easily and sliced beautifully . Sprinkled with powdered sugar.

I have made this every Thanksgiving for years. I use yogurt instead of sour cream due to preference. To those who says it’s too dry, maybe it’s over baked because mine has always been super moist. To those that say the batter is too thick, it’s never bothered me but if it does you, add a tablespoon of milk. It’s a great recipe & my family enjoys eating it while watching the Thanksgiving Day parade!
I have made this ar least 25 times. Every one loves it. My original recipe called for 1 cup of butter. I have made it both ways. DELICIOUS!
Wonderful holiday cake. I used more relish and increased cooking time to 35 min.

This is a moist coffee cake with great texture and flavor. I added a powder sugar glaze with a hint of the almond extract to give it a little jazz, but it is really sweet enough. My husband loved it but requested that when I make it again to add walnuts, which I think would be a nice addition.

Making this the second time. Thought I did something wrong last time, the batter was so thick. I had used a hand mixer the first time, This time I pulled out the big guns...the Kitchen aid..lol...batter is thick, needs to be spooned in. Used a whole can of cranberries this time..my husband's request...more cranberries!! Not worried about this one, the first was excellent! YUM!!!!
